subject: Availability guarantee & billing-offset framework (CloudCrest)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cloudcrest.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudcrest.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify uptime %, credits and billing offsets for launch

Hi Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our dev team was impressed with the latency graphs. Procurement has one gating question before we move to PO: how does Redwood intend to apply monthly service credits versus billing offsets? CloudCrest needs credits to be visible on invoices (not as refunds) and wants a clear cap for exposure during the first 90 days of launch.

Specifically:
- Can you confirm the standard availability guarantee you propose for the US region?
- Will credits be applied as an offset to the invoice that month or do you issue a separate credit memo?
- Is there a cap on monthly credits (percentage or dollar cap)? CloudCrest is worried about an open-ended liability during ramp.

We attached our standard procurement checklist; happy to review a short bullet-point answer first and then we can redline the SLA.

Best,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Procurement, CloudCrest
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cloudcrest.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime %, credits and billing offsets for launch

Marta — thanks for the clear questions. Looping Ben (sales ops) and Laura (legal) so we can align on contract language. Answers below are high-level (we can mirror these into the redline):

1) Availability guarantee: for hosted API we propose 99.95% regional uptime as our standard baseline for US production workloads. For pilot/launch customers we can offer a phased baseline: 99.9% for the first 30 days, moving to 99.95% thereafter, provided usage stays within the expected commit.

2) Credits vs billing offsets: Redwood issues service credits that are applied as a billing offset on the next invoice by default (credit memo applied against upcoming invoice). We do not issue cash refunds for SLA credits unless otherwise contractually agreed. Credits will appear as a line item: "SLA Service Credit (month)" and reduce the total due.

3) Monthly cap: our standard cap is either 25% of the monthly invoice or a $250k cap, whichever is lower. For early-stage pilots where usage is smaller, we can set a fixed cap (e.g., $10k) for the first 90 days — this is intended to limit Redwood's exposure while we stabilize ramp.

Operational carve-outs to flag (we recommend adding to the SLA): maintenance windows (we propose a weekly 2-hour maintenance window with prior notice), scheduled model-rollout pauses, and a batched-inference burst window carve-out for deployments that use continuous batching (we exclude short-term degradation during automated batch compaction operations).

I attached a short redline (SLA_Schedule_v2_redline.pdf) that shows the phased baseline and the proposed cap. Ben / Laura — any notes to add from pricing/legal?

Thanks,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cloudcrest.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime %, credits and billing offsets for launch

Kim — quick commercial note from my side. Two practical negotiation points that usually get us to yes with mid-market procurement teams:

- dual-track cap: set a low fixed cap for month 1-3 (e.g., $10k) then revert to percentage/dollar whichever-lower cap thereafter. This gives CloudCrest predictability during ramp and limits Redwood exposure while usage grows.
- single-invoice application: apply credits as offsets on the next invoice; if there is no subsequent invoice within 60 days, we carry forward the credit for up to 6 months. That prevents open credits being forgotten and avoids issuing refunds.

Also, on the batched-inference carve-out — clarify that the carve-out is limited to automated batch compaction periods and not to sustained performance regressions; sustained issues still trigger credits. I suggest the redline include a definition: "batch compaction window — automated global compaction events up to 30 minutes per day per region".

Laura — if legal is comfortable I can include the dual-track cap and carry-forward language in the next redline.

-ben
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cloudcrest.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime %, credits and billing offsets for launch

Marta — copying the key contractual points we'll reflect in the SLA redline:

1) Phased availability baseline: 99.9% (days 0–30) -> 99.95% (day 31 onward) subject to committed usage thresholds.

2) Credit calculation: monthly credit = (Monthly Fee) * (Downtime % / 100). Example table will be in redline. Credits are non-cash and applied as invoice offsets (credit memo) on the following invoice; carry-forward allowed up to 6 months if no invoice is due.

3) Cap structure: dual-track as discussed — fixed cap for launch months then standard capped at the lower of 25% of monthly invoice or $250k. We'll include a clean definition for "monthly invoice" to avoid disputes.

4) Carve-outs and definitions: maintenance windows (weekly 2-hour window with 48-hour notice), emergency maintenance (exceptions with post-notice), and a narrowly scoped batch-compaction carve-out (no more than 30 minutes/day/region). Sustained regressions beyond these windows will trigger credits.

5) Evidence & dispute: Redwood will provide incident reports and timeline; CloudCrest can open a dispute within 30 days of credit issuance. If both parties agree, credits will be applied retroactively to the month in question.

Next steps: we will produce a redline that replaces the generic remedy table with the example calculation and the dual-cap wording. Ben will push updated commercial terms to the HubSpot deal and I will upload the redline to DocuSign if the language is accepted.

Marta — can you confirm CloudCrest is OK with credits as invoice offsets (not cash) and the proposed dual-track cap approach? If yes, we'll send the redline by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
